opportunities.title: Move 7 projects off an end-of-life runtime
opportunities.finding: CloudWars.Common/CloudWars.Common.csproj (net45), CloudWars.DataAccess/CloudWars.DataAccess.csproj (net45), CloudWars.Engine/CloudWars.Engine.csproj (net40), CloudWars.Entities/CloudWars.Entities.csproj (net45), CloudWars.Game/CloudWars.Game.csproj (net45), CloudWars.Glue/CloudWars.Glue.csproj (net40), CloudWars.SpaceBattle/CloudWars.SpaceBattle.csproj (net45) — end of support 2016-01-12 (target out of support; runs in place on 4.6.2+/4.8, which remain supported).
opportunities.consequence: No vendor security fixes are available for these projects at all. A disclosed vulnerability has no remediation path other than in-house patching.
opportunities.action: Retarget to a supported runtime. Do this after characterization tests exist, so the retarget is provable.

opportunities.title: Pin behaviour in 3 untested areas
opportunities.finding: No test reaches CloudWars.Game, CloudWars.Engine, CloudWars.Glue.
opportunities.consequence: No change to these areas — including a security patch — can be shown to be safe before release. This blocks every other improvement.
opportunities.action: Start with the 2 area(s) rated "likely pinnable" (CloudWars.Engine, CloudWars.Glue); they need no refactoring first.

opportunities.title: Resolve the legacy package manifest against a live advisory feed
opportunities.finding: Dependencies are declared in pre-SDK `packages.config` manifests, which the standard tooling cannot check for currency or advisories.
opportunities.consequence: The security posture of these dependencies is unknown — not clean. "0 advisories" here means "not checked".
opportunities.action: Resolve every pinned version against nuget.org (or an offline mirror), then migrate the manifests to PackageReference so future checks are automatic.

opportunities.title: Capture what Cloudancy knows
opportunities.finding: 2 core file(s) are ≥80% one author's work (CloudWars.Game/Web.config 100%; CloudWars.Game/CloudWars.Game.csproj 83%).
opportunities.consequence: If that person becomes unavailable, the reasoning behind these files is unrecoverable — and it is the reasoning, not the code, that migrations depend on.
opportunities.action: Interview now and record the answers as durable knowledge entries. This is the cheapest and most perishable item in any plan.

opportunities.title: Entity Framework 6 or earlier → Entity Framework Core
opportunities.consequence: requires a data-layer migration; usually the largest single item
opportunities.action: Plan the replacement as part of the runtime move; requires a data-layer migration; usually the largest single item.

opportunities.title: ASP.NET MVC (System.Web) → ASP.NET Core MVC
opportunities.consequence: the web host and pipeline change; controllers largely survive
opportunities.action: Plan the replacement as part of the runtime move; the web host and pipeline change; controllers largely survive.

opportunities.title: ASP.NET Web API 2 → ASP.NET Core controllers
opportunities.consequence: route and formatter configuration is rewritten
opportunities.action: Plan the replacement as part of the runtime move; route and formatter configuration is rewritten.

opportunities.title: Extract seams in CloudWars.Game
opportunities.finding: 61 I/O touch points across 38 source files (database 1, network 11, time 44, globals 5)
opportunities.consequence: Time, network and database calls made inline cannot be substituted in a test, so this area's behaviour cannot be pinned as written.
opportunities.action: Introduce injection points for the clock and external calls — the minimum change that makes the area testable, done before any behaviour change.

opportunities.title: Plan the exit from 6 maintenance-only targets
opportunities.finding: net8.0 receive security fixes only, with no new platform work.
opportunities.consequence: Every year on a maintenance target widens the gap to the supported platform and raises the eventual cost of the move.
opportunities.action: Schedule the upgrade as a funded phase rather than letting it arrive as an incident.

opportunities.title: Confirm the version policy for Needletail.DataAccess
opportunities.finding: Needletail.DataAccess is used in 3 areas (3 references).
opportunities.consequence: A shared component pinned to an old version means every fix made upstream has to be re-made here, or is simply missing.
opportunities.action: Compare the pinned version against the component's current release and decide, explicitly, whether to track it.

opportunities.title: Triage 4 author notes left in the code
opportunities.finding: 4 TODO/HACK/NOTE markers remain in the source.
opportunities.consequence: Each is a note from an author to a future maintainer about work they knew was unfinished. A static survey cannot tell which were resolved elsewhere.
opportunities.action: Triage them with the authors: resolve in code, or record an explicit decision to accept each one.

opportunities.title: DotNetOpenAuth → a maintained OpenID Connect library
opportunities.consequence: the project is unmaintained; auth flows must be re-verified
opportunities.action: Plan the replacement as part of the runtime move; the project is unmaintained; auth flows must be re-verified.

opportunities.title: jQuery 1.x → a current front-end approach
opportunities.consequence: front-end work, independent of the server migration
opportunities.action: Plan the replacement as part of the runtime move; front-end work, independent of the server migration.

opportunities.title: Newtonsoft.Json → System.Text.Json
opportunities.consequence: mechanical for simple payloads; attribute-heavy models need review
opportunities.action: Plan the replacement as part of the runtime move; mechanical for simple payloads; attribute-heavy models need review.
